requirements.text: Access to administrator-level OS accounts is restricted to the maximum extent possible; usage is controlled, monitored, and only permitted for relevant activities; least-privilege used otherwise.
Logins with built-in administrator accounts are not permitted except when specifically needed; individual accounts / escalation (sudo) are used instead.
Break-glass account usage is strictly controlled (safe-stored password, authorisation before retrieval) and monitored; password changed after use.
Individual administrator-level account access and usage are logged (in line with / as part of Control 6.4).
Administrator-level passwords are tightly controlled with physical access controls when physically recorded.
Systems disallow built-in admin logins except maintenance mode; apply to bridging servers. (Optional Enhancements)
Secure the virtualisation/cloud platform, virtual machines, and supporting virtual infrastructure (e.g. firewalls) to the same level as physical systems.

The same security requirements apply to the platform/VMs as to other systems: secure-zone location, privileged-access restrictions, login/password policies, security updates, restriction of internet access.
Vulnerability scanning is performed on Swift-related VMs and, when possible, on the platform.
The platform systems are subject to physical protection preventing unauthorised physical access.
VM isolation is ensured on the platform to prevent lateral movement out of a VM (to other VMs / the hypervisor / bypassing network controls).
Filtering/inspection of network flows reaching Swift-related VMs is performed, preferably external to the platform or enforced at the hypervisor level.
If isolation is ensured, hosted VMs maintain their own security classification.
When MFA is implemented for interactive access to Swift VM OSes (per 4.2), MFA is not mandatory at the platform-management level.
When relying on a third party for the platform, engage the third party to obtain reasonable comfort the objective is met.
Apply the control to all bridging servers used for back-office<->Swift data exchange. (Optional Enhancement)
All general-purpose and dedicated operator PCs, and systems within the secure zone, have controlled direct internet access in line with business.
General-purpose internet browsing (incl. e-mail) from systems within the secure zone is not permitted.
Internet access from systems within the secure zone is highly restricted and ideally should be blocked.
When possible, activities requiring the Internet are conducted outside the secure zone.
If internet access is needed from the secure zone, grant only to allowlisted URL destinations through a proxy with content inspection and blocking/filtering; outbound-initiated connections only.
The jump server does not have internet access.
Control internet access on general-purpose operator PCs used to reach the service provider / connector / browser GUI.
Control access via one of: remote-desktop/VM solution; allowlisted-URL proxy (outbound-only, content inspection); Web Gateway with denylist.
Alternative: enforce a jump server with no internet access combined with MFA (per control 4.2).
Internet access from middleware server / virtualisation platform is highly restricted/blocked. (Advisory)
If needed from those systems, allowlisted-URL proxy with content inspection. (Advisory)
Apply the control to all bridging servers used for back-office<->Swift data exchange. (Optional Enhancement)
All HW/SW inside the secure zone and on operator PCs are within vendor support, upgraded with mandatory updates, and have had security updates promptly applied.
Vendor support: software/hardware within the vendor's supported life-cycle; maintenance/licensing contracts in place.
Mandatory software updates are applied.
Security updates are promptly applied, aligned to assessed risk.
Security hardening is conducted and maintained on all in-scope components (reduce attack surface via least privilege).
Systems are hardened per vendor / industry (CIS, DISA STIG, NIST) / local security-configuration guidance.

Minimum hardening: change default passwords; disable unnecessary accounts; disable/restrict unnecessary services, ports, protocols; remove unnecessary software; restrict physical ports; set auto-lock; adjust vulnerable default configurations.
Deviations from the hardening baseline are documented with justification and mitigations.
Systems are maintained secure (checked at least twice per year; secure settings re-applied).
Application allowlisting on the OS; apply to bridging servers. (Optional Enhancement)
Confidentiality, integrity, and authentication mechanisms protect data exchanged between Swift components and the back-office first hops they connect to.
Inventorise back-office<->Swift flows and assess each for confidentiality/integrity/authenticity.
End-to-end data-level protection (e.g. AES-GCM LAU, XML DSIG) with recipient authentication and replay prevention.
For direct point-to-point connectivity, a secure protocol ensuring authentication/integrity/confidentiality, e.g. LAU + confidentiality, authenticated API over TLS, or two-way TLS.
Per-leg protection where bridging servers are used, and the bridging servers are themselves secured.
Define a risk-based plan to secure/migrate flows not yet protected.
Secure protocols use current cryptographic algorithms (AES, ECDHE) with adequate key lengths.
Credentials and private/bilateral keys used to secure flows are protected (e.g. KMS).
Legacy direct back-office flows. (Advisory now; mandatory in ~v2028)
The confidentiality and integrity of interactive operator sessions into the secure zone / to service-provider Swift applications are safeguarded.
All interactive sessions are protected by a cryptographic protocol (e.g. ssh, https with one-way TLS).
Protocols use current cryptographic algorithms (AES, ECDHE) with adequate key lengths.
Operator/admin/maintenance sessions have an inactivity lock-out limiting the session to the minimal necessary time frame.
If not implemented at the application level, the inactivity lock-out is implemented at the OS level or on the jump server.
Communication between the jump server and Swift components/underlying systems is protected by a secure mechanism (one-way or two-way TLS).
Apply to all bridging servers. (Optional Enhancement)
Secure-zone systems are scanned for vulnerabilities at OS and application level using an up-to-date reputable tool; results are acted upon.
Scanning is performed at least annually or after any significant change (quarterly/monthly/real-time recommended).
Reputable, updated tools; appropriate scan type (e.g. credentialed); scan credentials protected; safeguards to limit operational impact.
Scanning outcomes are documented (restricted access) and analysed for remediation (e.g. applying updates per 2.2).
MFA is used for interactive user access to Swift-related components/applications and operating-system accounts.
MFA principles: two distinct factors, second-factor device distinct from first, AAL2 guidance.
MFA on ≥ 1 authentication stage for admins/end users accessing Swift apps, the HSM, the hosting system, or externally exposed firewalls (jump server, operator PC login).
MFA for remote user administrative access (generally VPN authentication).
The MFA authentication system is preferably located within the secure zone.
Authentication factors are individually assigned (individual accountability).
If SSO (e.g. SAML) is implemented, a second factor is still required.
MFA must be used when accessing service-provider-operated Swift components.
Recorded passwords are stored in a protected physical or logical location, with access restricted on a need-to-know basis.
Passwords on physical media are protected (sealed tamper-evident envelope, safe, logging access to the storage location).
Passwords stored logically are protected by encryption-at-rest or obfuscation (no plaintext storage).
Logical storage has authenticated access with access logging (in line with / as part of Control 6.4).
Passwords are not recorded in user manuals or other operational means unless stored per the guidance.
If emergency access is granted, the password is changed immediately thereafter.
Passwords are not hardcoded in scripts or other software code.
Safe certification (UL/EN); apply to bridging servers. (Optional Enhancement)
